n: In the darkness, a voice is heard throughout the land, by everyone at once.

f.w: a voice heard

n: The voice cries “Wo” three times: to this people and to the whole earth unless they repent. The devil and his angels rejoice over the dead, who fell because of their sins. The Lord does not delight in their destruction.

f.w: the devil laugheth
wo
f.g: Old spelling of “woe”: grief or calamity.

n: The speaker takes responsibility: He burned the great city of Zarahemla and its inhabitants.

f.w: Zarahemla

n: He sank the city of Moroni into the sea.

f.w: Moroni

n: He buried Moronihah, hiding its wickedness from His sight so that the blood of murdered prophets would no longer cry out against them. This phrase repeats throughout the list.

f.w: the blood of the prophets and the saints

n: He sank the city of Gilgal and buried its people in the earth.

f.w: Gilgal
f.g: A Nephite city sharing its name with an important site in ancient Israel.

n: Onihah, Mocum, and a Nephite city called Jerusalem were covered by water to hide their wickedness.

f.w: the city of Jerusalem
f.g: A New World city named after the old, built by Lamanites and Amalekites.

n: Gadiandi, Gadiomnah, Jacob, and Gimgimno were sunk, with hills and valleys formed in their place.
Jacobugath, city of “king” Jacob’s people, was burned because its secret murders and combinations exceeded the wickedness of the whole earth. They had destroyed the peace and government of the land.

f.w: king Jacob
secret murders and combinations

n: Laman, Josh, Gad, and Kishkumen were burned because they cast out and stoned the prophets God sent.

f.w: Kishkumen
f.g: A city apparently named after the founder of the Gadianton band.

n: These cities had driven out every righteous person, leaving none to preserve them, so He sent fire. The pattern Samuel warned of came true.

f.w: there were none righteous among them
cry unto me from the ground

n: Many great destructions came on the land because of wickedness and abominations.
Then the tone shifts from judgment to invitation. To the survivors, spared because they were more righteous: won’t you return, repent, and be converted so I can heal you?

f.w: that I may heal you

n: Whoever comes to Him will have eternal life. His “arm of mercy” is stretched out, and He will receive anyone who comes.

f.w: mine arm of mercy is extended towards you

n: The speaker identifies Himself: Jesus Christ, the Son of God, Creator of heaven and earth, one with the Father from the beginning, through whom the Father is glorified.

f.w: I am Jesus Christ the Son of God
I am in the Father, and the Father in me
I created the heavens and the earth

n: He came to His own people, and they rejected Him, fulfilling the scriptures about His coming.

f.w: my own received me not

n: To all who receive and believe on Him, He gives power to become sons and daughters of God. Redemption comes through Him, and the law of Moses is fulfilled in Him.

f.w: to become the sons of God
in me is the law of Moses fulfilled

n: He is the light and life of the world, Alpha and Omega, the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, meaning He is the beginning and the end.

f.w: the light and the life of the world
Alpha and Omega

n: Animal sacrifices and burnt offerings are now done away, since they pointed to His sacrifice, which is complete.

f.w: your sacrifices and your burnt offerings shall be done away

n: The new sacrifice is a broken heart and a contrite spirit. Those who offer it, He will baptize with fire and the Holy Ghost, as happened to converted Lamanites who did not even realize it.

f.w: a broken heart and a contrite spirit
baptize with fire and with the Holy Ghost

n: He came to redeem the world and save it from sin.

f.w: to save the world from sin

n: Whoever repents and comes to Him as a little child, He will receive, for the kingdom of God belongs to such. For them He laid down His life and took it up again. He calls the ends of the earth to come and be saved.

f.w: as a little child
laid down my life, and have taken it up again
